title: Folk horror and old gods
description: Folk horror, living traditions, and places where the old story is still in force.
label: Ritual and place

showReasons.old-gods-of-appalachia: A long-running regional mythology gives every new story the weight of something older underneath it.
showReasons.the-silt-verses: Institutional faith and folk horror become a full political world rather than a one-off scare.
showReasons.the-town-whispers: Small-town scale makes folklore feel local, intimate, and impossible to leave behind.
showReasons.the-secret-of-st-kilda: An isolated island, cult pressure, and supernatural danger put old beliefs at the center.
showReasons.the-milkman-of-st-gaffs: A Lovecraftian village turns ritual and social order into the threat.
showReasons.the-wyrd-side: New Weird and folk-horror signals make it a compact route when you want strangeness without a huge back catalogue.
showReasons.hi-nay: Filipino supernatural tradition and a babaylan family put inherited knowledge and place at the center of the danger.
showReasons.the-love-talker: Appalachian disappearances and an isolated community make folk horror a question of place, secrecy, and inherited fear.
showReasons.petrified: Tales of ordinary people meeting the supernatural in a darker Ireland give the route a contemporary folk-horror branch.
